EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
Theon Design Unveils New Bespoke Porsche 911 Build, Rocks F1-Grade Carbon Fiber and 419 HP
65 photos
Photo: Theon Design
It took 18 months for this collaboration to take shape in the form of a gorgeous bespoke air-cooled 911, but judging by the results, I'd say it was worth the wait. You're looking at a 419-hp 4.0L coupe with an Oak Green Neo Metallic finish and a total weight of just 1,150 kg (2,535 lbs). That's 364 hp per metric ton.
This thing also packs selectable engine maps and a G50 five-speed manual gearbox, while the previously-mentioned semi-active dampers, bespoke spring rates, and wheels all combine to offer more precise handling and better ride compliance. Way better for UK roads than stock.
In terms of construction, the car's exterior bodywork, bumper and lower sill panels are all formed from carbon fiber, and this includes various trim panels. Altogether, we're talking about a roughly 300 kg (661 lbs) weight loss regimen.
Visually, I already mentioned the Oak Green Neo Metallic (an updated version of the classic Oak Green Metallic), but not how well it's complemented by the champagne Porsche script and matching exterior details. Even the wheels are rocking this hue - as are the brake discs and calipers.
Meanwhile, the 4.0L engine also produces 322 lb-ft (437 Nm) of torque, which may not sound like a lot, but trust me, it's enough for something that weighs this little. According to Theon Design , this car can accelerate from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in about 4 seconds flat. That's air-cooled heaven right there.
Moving along to the interior, highlights include the Beechwood semi-aniline and nubuck leather upholstery, champagne detailing, Recaro CS seats, new window switches, a fully electric heating and air-conditioning system, and more.
"As with every commission Theon Design undertakes, this project began by listening to what the client wanted – not just how they wanted their car to look, but how they wanted it to feel. That informed every aspect of the development program, from the engine, transmission, and brake package to spring rates, damper calibration, and steering response," stated Theon Design co-founder, Adam Hawley.
Photo: Theon Design "Throughout the eighteen-month development period, we spoke regularly with the client, involving them in all the decisions that would affect the car’s character. From the first conversation to the final sign-off drive, collaboration is key and ensures that the ownership experience is every bit as personal and rewarding as the design."
All this sounds pretty good, right? Well, something even more special is taking shape in the upcoming Theon R - meant to be the company's most hardcore interpretation of the air-cooled 911 . It'll put down over 500 hp while utilizing motorsport-derived technology and weighing less than 1,000 kg (2,200 lbs). It should make for an amazing driver's car, so stay tuned!
But what do you guys think? Would you rather drive a custom air-cooled 911 on the weekends, or something a little more... substantial ?
